title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Aurora Payments
summary: Quarterly renewal and expansion check-in. Customer is interested in a 12-month contract extension, increasing dedicated capacity for peak payment processing, and adding a EU region. Discussed pricing tiers, regional availability, SOC2/KMS concerns, benchmarking, and timeline for procurement.
next_steps: Maya - send updated pricing for 12-month reserved capacity + EU region add-on by 2027-10-07
Liam - share SOC2 report, network diagram, and KMS integration notes by 2027-10-03
Schedule benchmark run in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 with Aurora payment traces (Samir + Liam) target 2027-10-05
Maya & Karen - coordinate procurement timeline and required PO docs, target signing week of 2027-10-11
action_items: Maya - draft contract addendum for 12-month extension and send to Karen (due 2027-10-10)
Liam - prepare benchmark plan and test script for payment flows (due 2027-10-04)
Samir - provide sample traffic profile and peak TPS numbers (due 2027-10-02)
Olivia - set up follow-up call for pricing review (due 2027-10-06)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-30
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Olivia Reyes (Redwood CSM); Ravi Kapoor (CTO, Aurora), Elena Morales (VP Eng), Samir Gupta (Infra Lead), Karen Liu (Procurement), Jordan Price (SRE)

Summary: quick check in on renewal and expansion. Aurora wants to move to a longer term committed contract and add capacity in EU region for PSD2/residency. Also wants clarity on SOC2/KMS/VPC and run performance benchmarks.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for doing this, I know schedules are tight. quick roll call - we're Maya and Liam from Redwood, Olivia's here for post-sales and follow up.
[00:12] Ravi: hey Maya, hi Liam, thanks. Elena, Samir and Karen on our side. we wanted to go over renewal options and talk through capacity and regions.
[00:26] Maya: great. high level - you mentioned earlier you wanted to extend to 12 months and add EU region, and bump dedicated capacity for peak windows, is that right?
[00:34] Elena: yeah that's the ask. we've been happy with latency/availability in us-east but with EU customers we need eu-west presence for data residency and to meet regulator expectations.
[00:46] Liam: ok makes sense. quick question for Samir - can you remind us of your peak TPS and KV cache size? iirc you were seeing spikes up to 1.8k TPS during promos, and long seqs for reconciliation.
[01:03] Samir: yeah rough numbers - 1.5k sustained, 1.8k burst, typical sequence lengths vary, some reconciles push up to 6k tokens because they batch several transactions. our KV cache footprint is around 80GB active.
[01:18] Maya: thanks, that's helpful. for capacity, we can propose a reserved pool that covers sustained throughput and a burst buffer for spikes. we have a few options - 8x A100 equiv units, 12x, or 16x depending on how much headroom you want.
[01:34] Jordan: are those actual GPUs or inference units? we need to map to our cost model.
[01:41] Liam: it's reserved capacity expressed as GPU-equivalent slots for dedicated. billing is monthly commit but we can structure the add-on for eu as a regional replica so you have separate pools. note, quantization and batch tuning reduce effective cost per token.
[01:57] Ravi: what kind of latency differences do you typically see cross-region? we can't have EU customers routed through us-east for PII reasons.
[02:06] Liam: if we deploy in eu-west, your latencies should be within the same ballpark - maybe a 10-20ms variance depending on sequence length. the bigger factor is cold start and KV cache locality, which is why we recommend local KV cache pre-warming for critical flows.
[02:24] Elena: ok - SOC2 and KMS questions: procurement wants the attestation and details about key management, and whether Redwood Privet (sic) supports customer-managed keys.
[02:34] Maya: yes - Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integration; for hosted/dedicated we integrate with cloud KMS. we'll share the SOC2 doc and a network diagram. liam will attach KMS notes.
[02:47] Samir: one quick security: if we go with a regional dedicated pool, can we keep traffic on a VPC peering path and avoid egress through public internet?
[02:56] Liam: yes, we support VPC peering and private link options. there may be a short setup window for peering and firewall rules. Olivia can coordinate the onboarding checklist.
[03:09] Karen: procurement timeline - we need final pricing and contract language by mid-october to get PO in before our fiscal cutoff.
[03:18] Maya: understood, target week of Oct 11 for signature. we'll prioritize a pricing addendum and get it to you by Oct 7.
[03:26] Elena: on pricing, can you show a delta for reserved vs on-demand? and what's the discount for a 12-month commit plus a regional add-on?
[03:36] Maya: yes. high-level: reserved committed capacity gives ~35% unit discount vs on-demand; 12-month adds another ~5% if you commit to a minimum base. regional replicas are priced as a percentage add-on - typically 20% of base reserved given the additional infra and redundancy. i'll put exact numbers in the addendum.
[03:54] Ravi: are there any penalties for scaling down mid-contract? e.g., we might need to reduce after a seasonal burst.
[04:03] Maya: we can include a quarterly true-up clause; reserved commitments are for capacity but we can add a limited-downscale window once per quarter with pro-rated adjustments. we'll include flexible burst credits to handle short spikes so you don't have to overcommit.
[04:19] Jordan: about benchmarking - we want to run our payment flows against Redwood Dedicated to validate latency and cost at scale. what's the process?
[04:26] Liam: we can provision a short-lived benchmark cluster - a 'pilot' dedicated pool - and run your traces. we'll need Samir's traffic profile and a few sample payloads. aim for 48-72 hour run. results will include p50/p95/p99 and token cost estimates.
[04:43] Samir: i'll dump a week of anonymized traces and a peak-day sample. will share to liam by monday.
[04:50] Liam: perfect. we'll prepare a test plan and a script - i'll send that today.
[04:58] Speaker 1: (mumble) one more thing on model selection - are you guys on the current redwood catalog for our production model?
[05:06] Maya: yes you're on rwd-2027-v2 for gen and rwd-emb-1 for embeddings. we can discuss model variants for eu and cost-optimized quantized variants.
[05:18] Elena: is quantized still safe for us? payment text integrity is important.
[05:24] Liam: quantized models we recommend for generic flows. for sensitive reconciliation tasks we suggest FP16 or mixed precision to avoid regressions; we'll validate in the benchmark.
[05:36] Karen: legal will need clause on data retention and audit logs - we saw in the console there is token-level logs, can we export them for internal audits?
[05:46] Olivia: yes, we have export hooks and long-term retention as an add-on. also audit logs with SSO and RBAC controls. we'll send the doc.
[05:55] Ravi: we also wanted to compare the Redwood offer to some pitches from MegaCloud AI and NimbusML - they offered an integrated endpoint but their latency was higher for our long sequences. any differentiation we should call out?
[06:08] Maya: our focus is predictable inference economics and KV caching for long sequences; that tends to give you better cost/latency for long reconciliation flows versus generic endpoints. we'll include benchmark comparisons where available, though exact apples-to-apples is tricky.
[06:23] Elena: ok, can you also include a note on support SLAs for dedicated - response times and escalation paths?
[06:31] Olivia: we offer a 4-hour P1 initial response for dedicated customers with optional 1-hour paid SLA. escalation goes to the platform reliability team; we'll include the runbook.
[06:43] Samir: operationally, how do rollouts work? we need canary behavior and automatic fallback to smaller models if the pool is degraded.
[06:52] Liam: rollouts use per-route policies - you can do canary percent, A/B testing, auto-fallback to a compatible model variant and region, and tracing. you can pin by version and set automatic fallback rules.
[07:05] Jordan: good. on telemetry, will we get token-level cost metrics by route? that's critical for our product managers.
[07:12] Olivia: yes, console gives per-route token cost, latency breakdowns, and we can grant view rights to PMs with RBAC.
[07:22] Ravi: great. let's talk timeline: procurement needs pricing and contract text, engineering needs benchmarks and KMS docs. can we summarize milestones?
[07:31] Maya: milestone 1: pricing addendum and contract draft (Maya) by Oct 7. milestone 2: KMS/SOC2/security docs (Liam) by Oct 3. milestone 3: benchmark run (Samir + Liam) scheduled for Oct 5 window. milestone 4: finalize and sign week of Oct 11.
[07:49] Karen: that fits our fiscal window. if we get the addendum by Oct 7 we'll have time to route it through legal.
[07:56] Elena: one more technical - for EU deployment, is data at rest in EU? we need assurances for residency.
[08:04] Liam: yes, with a regional dedicated pool and local KV cache, data at rest and logs can be configured to remain in the region. we'll include data residency notes in the security doc.
[08:16] Ravi: about backup and DR across regions - if eu-west goes down, is there a cold failover to us-east? what's RTO?
[08:25] Liam: we support cross-region failover but you'll need to accept that data residency constraints may mean some re-run steps; RTO depends on how quickly you want to accept cross-region replication. typical RTO for full failover is in hours; we can model an active-passive replication for faster failover. we'll include options.
[08:40] Speaker 2: (brief cross talk)
[08:43] Maya: ok i'm going to capture action items - Liam will share SOC2 and KMS notes and test plan, Samir will share traces. i'll deliver pricing and contract addendum. Olivia will set follow-up for Oct 6 for pricing review.
[09:00] Karen: quick contract question - any minimums for regional replica? we want to avoid being forced into a large commitment per region.
[09:08] Maya: regional replicas can be scoped; the addendum will show a baseline and optional scale tiers. you can start small and add capacity as needed, though discounts apply at higher commit levels.
[09:21] Elena: can we get a rough monthly cost estimate now so procurement has a number?
[09:26] Maya: ballpark: for 12-month commit with 12x GPU-equivalent dedicated pool + EU replica scaled at 30% of base, estimate ~$95k/month pre-discount; final will depend on model mix and token volume.
[09:42] Ravi: that's in the range - we'll review.
[09:47] Jordan: small ops question - do environment secrets for model ops stay in our KMS? we want no plaintext in Redwood control plane.
[09:55] Liam: yes - with customer-managed KMS, secrets are encrypted and keys are customer-controlled; we don't hold plaintext keys.
[10:03] Karen: perfect. we'll need a short exhibit for procurement that lists deliverables and acceptance criteria for the pilot.
[10:11] Maya: we'll attach a pilot exhibit to the addendum with acceptance criteria tied to p95 latency and throughput.
[10:18] Elena: okay that's helpful. any blockers on Redwood side?
[10:23] Liam: no blockers - just need the traces and your sign-off on test windows.
[10:29] Samir: i'll get traces and spike day by Monday.
[10:33] Olivia: i'll send calendar invites for the benchmark window and price review.
[10:38] Maya: sounds good. any last questions?
[10:41] Ravi: none from me. thanks everyone.
[42:10] Maya: thanks all - we'll follow up with docs and pricing. end.

Notes about transcript quality: some speaker attributions approximate, occasional words mis-transcribed (Redwood Privet = Redwood Private), and a few acronyms mistranscribed.
